findings.title: IDP-only sources are handed a combined-pool percentile but scored on the IDP-slice Hill master, so they vote ~48% of the anchor's value at the identical effective rank
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — scope curve routing
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md step 3/5: 'Scope-appropriate curve routing (cross-market -> GLOBAL, overall IDP -> IDP, everything else -> OFFENSE)'; the dlfIdp registry entry says shared-market ladder translation 'correctly calibrates DLF against the retail offense market'. Both together assert every source's contribution lands in one 0-9999 coordinate system.
findings.observed: `needs_shared_market_translation` rewrites an IDP-only source's rank into COMBINED-pool coordinates (dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsIdp raw rank 1 -> effective rank 34 for Aidan Hutchinson, the same slot idpTradeCalc gives him). `_percentile_denom_for_source` then divides by 500 (combined-pool N) and `_curve_for_source` routes by SCOPE to the IDP master (c=0.0830) which was fit on IDPTradeCalc's IDP-only slice. The two coordinate systems are inconsistent: at percentile 0.0661 the IDP master pays 5627 while the value-direct anchor on the same row pays 6444. Measured over the whole board the four IDP-scope rank-signal sources contribute a median 0.461/0.474/0.481/0.485 of idpTradeCalc's contribution on the same row. On offense — where source rank space and curve space agree — every source clusters at 0.87-1.08 of the anchor. Re-scoring the SAME percentiles through the GLOBAL master (the curve fit on the combined pool the ladder maps into) returns median ratios 0.92/1.32/1.29/0.95.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python3 docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/repro_blend.py  # then see docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/w02-measurements.json .idpCurveScaleMismatch
reproduction.expected: IDP-scope source contribution / idpTradeCalc contribution ~= 1.0 on the same row (as offense achieves)
reproduction.actual: median 0.4612 (dlfIdp), 0.4737 (dlfRookieIdp), 0.4806 (idpShow), 0.4845 (fantasyProsIdp)

numericProof.formula: V(p) = 9999 / (1 + (p/c)^s) evaluated at the SAME p for the IDP master vs the GLOBAL master

findings.userImpact: Every IDP row's 'multi-source consensus' is dragged down by a units error rather than by disagreement: three sources that rank Aidan Hutchinson their #1 IDP are shown, in the /rankings value-chain panel, as valuing him 13% below the one source that ranks him 34th. A user reads real disagreement where the sources actually agree exactly, and sells IDP assets into a board biased low.

priorFinding.note: Prior said '~48% of the IDP market at the same rank'. Independently measured 46.1-48.5% median over 605 source votes on the 2026-08-04 board, plus the GLOBAL-curve counterfactual that isolates the mechanism.

findings.whatWorks: The shared-market ladder translation itself is correct — it lands IDP rank 1 on exactly the combined-pool rank the anchor gives. Only the curve chosen afterwards is wrong.
findings.rootCause: `_curve_for_source` routes on `scope`, while `_percentile_denom_for_source` and the ladder both operate in combined-pool space. Scope is the wrong key: what determines the right curve is which POOL the effective rank lives in, and after `needs_shared_market_translation` that pool is the combined one.
findings.requiredRepair: Route any source whose effective rank has been ladder-translated into combined-pool space through the GLOBAL master (or, equivalently, key `_curve_for_source` on `sharedMarketTranslated`/`needs_rookie_translation` rather than on `scope`). Re-fit is not required — the GLOBAL master is already the combined-pool curve.
findings.dependencies: Fixing this changes 52 anchor ejections (W02-F002) and most of the 127 corridor clamps (W02-F003); those two findings should be re-measured after, not fixed independently.

findings.title: The Hampel filter ejects the designated IDP market anchor on 29.4% of Hampel-eligible IDP rows, and in 52 of 52 cases for being HIGH
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — per-player outlier rejection
findings.claimUnderTest: `_hampel_filter_per_player` docstring: 'catches the "FootballGuys is way off on this one player" case without dropping the whole source globally'. The registry calls idpTradeCalc 'the retail IDP authority and the backbone source'.
findings.observed: On the live board `idpTradeCalc` is Hampel-dropped on 52 IDP rows — 29.4% of the 177 IDP rows that carry >= 4 sources (17.7% of all 293 ranked IDP rows). Direction is not random: in 52/52 cases the anchor was ejected for sitting ABOVE the median of its peers. That is the exact signature of W02-F001 — the peers are on a ~2x compressed scale, so the correctly-scaled market anchor is the statistical outlier. Named victims include Maxx Crosby, T.J. Watt, Micah Parsons (via the same mechanism), Jalen Carter, Kyle Hamilton, Roquan Smith and Trey Hendrickson. Board-wide the filter drops 192 of 6,442 source votes (2.98%) across 168 of 800 rows (21.0%).

findings.title: The corridor clamp's per-bucket P90 machinery is inert — the 0.15 cap binds on 100% of clamps — and it rewrites 43.3% of ranked IDP rows to exactly idpTradeCalc x 0.85 or x 1.15
findings.subsystem: Core value blend — market corridor clamp
findings.claimUnderTest: `_apply_market_corridor_clamp` docstring: 'Band width is empirical — P90 of |final - market| / market computed within each confidence bucket'; the Phase-4c call site: 'Leaves 90% of the board untouched — only the tail outliers ... get pulled back to the band edge.' CLAUDE.md step 10: 'P90 drift band per confidence bucket, hard band cap 0.15'.
findings.observed: Measured on the live board the per-bucket P90 drifts are 0.4805 (medium, n=91), 0.5097 (low, n=173) and 0.5228 (high, n=29) — every one of them 3x the 0.15 asset-class cap. `cappedByMaxBand` is therefore true on 127 of 127 clamped rows: the percentile computation, the per-bucket split, the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_MIN_BUCKET_N` fallback and the `_MARKET_CORRIDOR_PERCENTILE` constant are all dead weight, and the live behaviour is a flat +/-15% band around one source. It does not leave 90% untouched: 127 of the 293 eligible rows (43.3%) are rewritten, mean move 464.7 points (28.9% of the pre-clamp value), max 110.9% (a value more than doubled). On all 127 the published `rankDerivedValue` equals `round(marketAnchor * (1 +/- 0.15))` to within 1 — i.e. the number a user sees is a pure function of a single source, with the other four contributing nothing. 126 of 127 anchor on `idpTradeCalc`; 1 anchors on `fantasyProsIdp` via the stage-2 fallback chain.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python3 -c "import json,collections;p=json.load(open('/tmp/full.json'));cl=[r for r in p['playersArray'] if r.get('marketCorridorClamp')];print(len(cl),collections.Counter((r['marketCorridorClamp']['bandPct'],r['marketCorridorClamp']['cappedByMaxBand']) for r in cl));print(sum(1 for r in cl if abs(round(r['marketCorridorClamp']['marketAnchor']*(1.15 if r['marketCorridorClamp']['direction']=='down' else 0.85))-r['rankDerivedValue'])<=1))"
reproduction.expected: a minority of clamps use the 0.15 cap; ~10% of eligible rows clamped; clamped value reflects the bucket's own empirical P90
reproduction.actual: 127/127 capped at 0.15; 43.3% of eligible rows clamped; 127/127 land exactly on anchor*(1+/-0.15)

findings.userImpact: On /rankings and in every trade engine, 127 IDP players carry a value that is arithmetically 0.85x or 1.15x one vendor's number. Nothing on the page says so — `marketCorridorClamp` is materialised onto the row by `buildRows` (frontend/lib/dynasty-data.js:1070) and rendered by no component. A user comparing our board to IDPTradeCalc believes they are seeing independent corroboration; they are seeing the same number scaled by a constant.

priorFinding.note: Prior said the cap binds on 100% of clamps. Reproduced (127/127) and extended with the clamp RATE (43.3% of eligible, against a docstring claiming 90% untouched), the magnitude distribution (mean 28.9%, max 110.9%), and the exactness proof that all 127 published values equal anchor*(1+/-0.15).

findings.whatWorks: The clamp is correctly scoped: 0 offense rows and 0 pick rows were clamped, matching CLAUDE.md's 'IDP rows only'. The `marketCorridorClamp` stamp is complete and honest in the payload.
findings.rootCause: Two independent bands were layered without checking whether the empirical one ever wins. It never does, because the drift distribution the P90 is measured over is itself inflated by W02-F001.
findings.requiredRepair: Either delete the P90/bucket machinery and document the band as a flat +/-15% policy, or fix W02-F001 (which should collapse the drift distribution) and re-measure whether a clamp is still needed at all. Whichever is chosen, surface the clamp on the row — a value that is a constant times one vendor's price must not render identically to a genuine 14-source blend.

findings.title: The blend is not monotone in a source's own vote: raising idpTradeCalc's contribution by 3% drops the pre-clamp blended value 25.8%
findings.claimUnderTest: Implicit and load-bearing everywhere downstream: a better source rank / higher source value produces a higher blended value. The count-aware mean-median blend and the alpha-shrinkage combine are both monotone by construction, which is what makes the property look guaranteed.
findings.observed: Holding Dallas Turner's four other source contributions fixed and sweeping idpTradeCalc's contribution, the pre-clamp blended value rises smoothly to 2502.3 at 3300, then falls to 1856.6 at 3400 — a 25.8% drop caused by a 3.0% INCREASE in one input, because the Hampel threshold crosses and the anchor is ejected. Above 3400 the blend is completely insensitive to the anchor (flat 1856.6 out to 5200). The composed post-clamp value happens to stay monotone on this row only because the clamp re-derives it from the ejected source; the blend itself — the number stamped as `_blendedValueUncapped` and used to price every unranked rookie and therefore every current-year pick via tethering — is discontinuous. Every other stage verified monotone: per-source `valueContribution` is strictly decreasing in effective rank with 0 inversions across all 21 sources once TE rows (where the premium deliberately repositions within the scale) are excluded.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-riskittogetthebrisket/0f0078ff-84f2-50d3-bce6-2bb1d1d8e920/scratchpad/e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; curl -s -b /tmp/c.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/full.json; python3 docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/repro_blend.py ; see docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W02/dallas-turner-sweep.json

findings.userImpact: A source revising a player UPWARD can move our board DOWN. Because `_blendedValueUncapped` is what the rookie pool is sorted by, a discontinuity there also reorders which rookie a current-year pick tethers to, so the instability propagates to the pick board.

priorFinding.note: The prior audit reported the anchor-ejection rate (A11-F01) but not that the ejection makes the blend a non-monotone function of its own inputs, nor that the blend is flat in the anchor above the ejection threshold.

findings.whatWorks: Every deterministic stage (Hill curve, count-aware blend, alpha-shrinkage, single-source haircut, clamp) is individually monotone; only the Hampel gate breaks it.
findings.rootCause: Hard-thresholded outlier rejection composed with an aggregator makes the composition a step function of every input.
findings.requiredRepair: Replace the hard drop with a continuous down-weight (e.g. Huber/Tukey weights on the same deviation statistic) so a source's influence tapers rather than vanishing at a threshold.
findings.dependencies: W02-F001 (the ejections it fires on)

findings.title: Ranks past the fixed 500-row reference collapse to one value: 440 rank-signal votes carry zero ordering information, including 164 of idpShow's 279
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md step 2: 'Percentile normalization against a FIXED 500-rank combined-pool reference (ranks past 500 clamp to the curve tail; this is deliberate top-500-board behavior)'.
findings.observed: `percentile_to_value` clamps p to [0,1], so every effective rank >= 500 evaluates at p=1.0 and returns the identical tail value. 743 of 6,442 source votes (11.5%) sit at p=1.0; 440 of those are on the rank->Hill path where the clamp actually destroys information. The effect is concentrated on IDP because the shared-market ladder pushes IDP ordinals deep into combined space: idpShow's raw ranks 146 through 344 — 199 distinct ordinal positions — all contribute exactly 594; fantasyProsIdp 146-211 and dlfIdp 146-170 likewise contribute 594; draftSharksIdp's raw ranks 100-315 all contribute exactly 1698. findings.title: Every trade the arbitrage finder returns is a 1-for-2; 1-for-1 candidates exist but rank 2,159th and 2-for-1 never qualifies at all
findings.claimUnderTest: finder.py generates three package shapes (_generate_1for1, _generate_2for1, _generate_1for2) and ranks them together by arbitrage_score.
findings.observed: 480 returned trades across all 12 teams: 480 are '1-for-2'. Zero 1-for-1, zero 2-for-1. Running find_trades for Jason with max_results=100000 yields 5,562 qualified trades — 5,399 1-for-2, 163 1-for-1, and ZERO 2-for-1 — and the first 1-for-1 appears at rank 2,159. The scoring function is the cause: board_gain_norm = board_delta / give_model divides by the give side only, so shrinking the give side to one asset inflates the dominant term (f_board_edge = board_gain_norm*50) without bound, while the entire counterweight is f_simplicity = -(pkg_size-2)*3 = -3.

reproduction.actual: Counter({'1-for-2': 5399, '1-for-1': 163}); first 1-for-1 at rank 2159; MAX_RESULTS=40

A user never sees a straight player-for-player swap or a consolidation offer, only 'give one good player, get two lesser ones' — the single shape that is hardest to get accepted and that structurally worsens roster-spot pressure in a 58-slot league.

priorFinding.note: Prior measured 98% of output in the 1-for-N direction; the live measurement is 100% of returned output (480/480) and 97.1% of qualified output (5399/5562). The 2-for-1 direction that the guards WERE written for produces zero qualifying trades, so those guards are dead in production.

findings.whatWorks: _deduplicate correctly collapses same-asset permutations; the multi-for-one guards (MULTI_FOR_ONE_MIN_RATIO, ELITE_MULTI_MIN_RATIO, PACKAGE_ANCHOR_MIN_PCT) are correctly implemented — they just guard a direction that never survives the output filter.
findings.rootCause: The normalizer in board_gain_norm is give_model, not (give_model+recv_model)/2 or max(); combined with a flat -3 simplicity penalty this makes score monotonically increasing in receive-side count.
findings.requiredRepair: Normalize board_delta against the larger of the two sides (or their mean), and/or reserve slots per package shape in the returned list so each shape gets representation. Either fix must be re-measured against the shape distribution above.

findings.title: Monte Carlo uncertainty is a hard-coded flat +/-15% band on zero live rows, and the 9999 clamp makes it understate an elite asset by 5.07%
findings.claimUnderTest: monte_carlo.py module docstring: 'Given side-A and side-B as lists of players, each with a valueBand from Phase 4 (p10, p50, p90)... Depends on: Phase 4 confidence intervals'. build_trade_player: 'Prefers the Phase 4 valueBand dict; falls back to +/-15% band'.
findings.observed: 0 of 1,092 playersArray rows carry a valueBand, so the fallback IS the production path for every asset — every player, pick and defender is drawn from an identical +/-15% triangle regardless of whether the board blended 1 source or 14 (effectiveSourceRanks ranges 0-14 across the contract). The frontend synthesizes the same +/-15% band client-side. Worse, _shifted() clamps to 9999 while the +15% leg is not, so for a top-of-board asset the upper half of the band is truncated and the sampled mean falls BELOW the board value: Brock Bowers (rankDerivedValue 9947) simulates at sideAMean 9441.9. No convergence diagnostic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned; ten identical calls give winProbA 0.0001-0.0003 and meanDelta -4455.2 to -4439.3.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w09-full.json'));print('rows with valueBand:',sum(1 for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('valueBand')),'of',len(d['playersArray']))" ; curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies-w09.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/trade/simulate-mc -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"sideA":[{"name":"Brock Bowers","rankDerivedValue":9947,"pos":"TE","team":"LV"}],"sideB":[{"name":"Jonathan Taylor","rankDerivedValue":6431,"pos":"RB","team":"IND"},{"name":"Patrick Mahomes","rankDerivedValue":7461,"pos":"QB","team":"KC"}]}' | python -c 'import json,sys;r=json.load(sys.stdin);print(r["sideAMean"], r["nSims"])'

reproduction.actual: rows with valueBand: 0 of 1092; sideAMean 9441.9

numericProof.formula: E[draw] = sum over segments of ((lo+hi)/2)*weight, using the piecewise-linear _triangular_draw quantile map

findings.userImpact: On /trade the MC panel says 'Side B came out ahead in 100% of 20,000 simulations'. That number is produced from an invented, uniform uncertainty and a mean that is 5% low for exactly the elite assets a trade usually hinges on. A user rejects an even trade because the simulator's fabricated distribution says it is not close.

priorFinding.note: Also confirms PRIOR-A09-F03 and PRIOR-A10-F02, which state the same defect from the constants and documentation angles. New here is the 9999-clamp bias: the fabricated band is not merely uninformative, it is directionally WRONG at the top of the board, understating the board value by 504 points (5.07%) with an analytic derivation that matches the live sideAMean to 1.1 points.

findings.whatWorks: The direction-symmetrization is real and effective (symmetryCheck.drift 0.0001, enforced true), the labelHint/disclaimer contract fields ARE returned by the backend, and run-to-run variance is genuinely small (meanDelta sd 5.1 on a magnitude of 4,447 over 10 runs at 100k sims) — the estimator is stable, it is just estimating a fabricated quantity.
findings.rootCause: The band producer (src/canonical/confidence_intervals) never stamps valueBand onto contract rows, so the documented input does not exist on any live row; the fallback was written as a degradation path and became the only path.

findings.title: The finder's 'high confidence' tier is structurally unreachable: it measures the scraper's 3-source site count against a 5-source baseline while the board blends up to 14
findings.claimUnderTest: finder.py: confidence = source_confidence * ktc_confidence with CONFIDENCE_SOURCE_BASELINE = 5 'Expected source count for full confidence'; _confidence_tier returns 'high' at >= 0.75.

All 480 returned trades across 12 teams are 'moderate' (244) or 'low' (236); 'high' appears zero times. The board's real blend count is on the contract rows: Brock Bowers has 12 effective post-Hampel sources while his _sites reads 3, and the contract's effectiveSourceRanks distribution runs to 14.

The label is uninformative in one direction and misleadingly pessimistic in the other, and the confidence multiplier (0.7 + 0.3*conf) applies a permanent 0.88 haircut to every score, so it also cannot reorder anything.

priorFinding.note: Prior called the tier 'a constant'. findings.title: Monte Carlo run-to-run variance is small but no convergence statistic is exposed, and the panel that calls it 404s through the Next origin
findings.claimUnderTest: Prompt section 15: run simulate-mc 10 times on the same input and measure variance; is convergence exposed; does simulate disagree with simulate-mc?
findings.observed: Variance is genuinely low — 10 identical calls give meanDelta in [-4455.2, -4439.3] (population sd 5.13 on a magnitude of 4,447, i.e. 0.12%), stdDelta in [1439.3, 1449.6], winProbA in [0.0001, 0.0003]. But no convergence statistic, standard error, confidence interval or seed echo is returned, so a caller cannot distinguish a stable 0.50 from a noisy one; the only diagnostic is symmetryCheck.drift, which measures ordering bias, not convergence. nSims is also reported as double the request (asked 50000, got 100000) because symmetrize sums the two directional passes (symmetrize.py:74) — the UI renders that as 'X% of 100,000 simulations'. simulate and simulate-mc do NOT disagree on value source: both prefer offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue for all-offense trades and agree at 4004 / -3945 respectively once the same inputs are used (the 59-point gap is entirely explained by the frontend sending effectiveValue while the backend simulate reads the row). Separately, POST /api/trade/simulate-mc and /api/trade/simulate return 404 through http://127.0.0.1:3000, which is the origin the page is served from — MonteCarloButton fetches the relative path, so the panel is dead outside a reverse-proxied deployment.

findings.title: src/nfl_data/realized_points.py disagrees with the league host on 36% of player-weeks: it never reads the six reception-distance rules, maps pass_int/pass_sack/fum_lost to nflverse columns that no longer exist, and has no kicker scoring at all
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_comparison/scoring_engine.py:6 — 'compute_weekly_points ... is already the single source of truth for Sleeper-format fantasy scoring'. CLAUDE.md — BDVM's baseline is 'realized nflverse PPG under the league's exact scoring'.
findings.observed: Scored 636 real 2025 player-weeks (nflverse rows) against the same 636 Sleeper host stat lines under the SAME live dynasty_main scoring_settings. Only 406 (63.8%) agree within 0.011. Three independent causes, each confirmed by decomposing individual players: (1) rec_0_4/rec_5_9/rec_10_19/rec_20_29/rec_30_39/rec_40p appear in neither _SIMPLE_KEYS nor the threshold-bonus list, costing 157.03 points across 197 rows — Stefon Diggs 2025 wk5 exact 30.100 vs realized 23.400, delta -6.700 = 0.34+4.02+2.34 exactly. (2) _SIMPLE_KEYS maps pass_int->'interceptions', pass_sack->'sacks', fum_lost->'fumbles_lost'; the 2025 unified nflverse release names them passing_interceptions, sacks_suffered and fumbles_lost_total, so stat_row.get returns None -> _num -> 0.0 and the key is skipped. Patrick Mahomes wk14 exact 0.823 vs realized 14.823, delta exactly +14.000 = 3 INT x 4.00 + 2 sacks x 1.00. Across the sample these three penalties are worth 208 points that are never charged. (3) No kicker key is read at all (fgm_yds 0.07, xpm 2.31, xpmiss -3.15, six fgmiss_* bands) although K is a starting slot; every kicker scores 0.000 (33/33 rows wrong, mean -9.251). Per-group agreement: IDP 312/350 (89.1%, mean -0.034 — this path is essentially correct), other 66/71, WR 11/64, TE 10/48, RB 4/32, QB 3/38 (mean +6.533), K 0/33 (mean -9.251).

reproduction.expected: 636/636 agree within 0.011 (the tolerance src/league_intel/scorer.py's own docstring sets)
reproduction.actual: 406/636 agree; QB mean +6.533, K mean -9.251, WR mean -1.558

inputs.reference: src/league_intel/scorer.score_stat_line, itself validated 1339/1339 vs Sleeper players_points

findings.userImpact: The direction is systematic, not random: QBs are over-scored by ~6.5 pts/week and pass-catchers under-scored by 0.8-1.6 pts/week, so any fundamental value built on this engine tilts the board toward QBs and away from WR/TE/RB. On /rankings the 'Fund gap' column and on /bdvm the entire value board are derived from it; on /league-comparison the positional-balance verdict a user reads to decide whether their league over-pays QBs is computed from the engine that over-pays QBs.

priorFinding.note: Confirms the reception-band half exactly (6 rules, WR most affected) and extends it with two causes that audit did not report: three dead nflverse column mappings worth +208 pts of uncharged QB penalties, and the complete absence of kicker scoring in a league that starts a K. Also partially confirms PRIOR-A24-F19 and refutes the implication in PRIOR-A22-F02 that IDP is the broken half — measured, IDP is the ONE group this engine gets right.

findings.whatWorks: The IDP path is correct and well-defended: the _SCORING_KEY_ALIASES derivation from sleeper_ingest.KEY_ALIASES resolves idp_pass_def->idp_pd and idp_qb_hit->idp_hit, _tackle_view reconstructs gamebook solo from the post-2025 columns, and the group agrees with the host at 89.1% with mean signed error -0.034.

findings.title: ADR-006's 'pure dot product, no stacking rules' claim independently reproduced against 1,339 host-scored player-weeks (max |delta| 0.005), and stacking answered on real host stat lines: pick-six charges -6.00, distance bonuses stack on the base reception, and one sack pays eight IDP categories
findings.claimUnderTest: src/league_intel/scorer.py:3-25 — 'a pure dot product over the keys shared between a player's weekly stat line and the league's scoring_settings ... No exclusions, no de-duplication, no special-casing ... reproduced Sleeper's own players_points exactly (|delta| <= 0.011) for 1,415 of 1,415 rostered player-weeks.'

Fetched the 2025 predecessor league (1180092661344120832) with its own scoring_settings plus GET /v1/league/.../matchups/{5,9,14} for host-awarded players_points and GET /v1/stats/nfl/regular/2025/{5,9,14} for the raw stat lines. score_stat_line reproduces the host on 1,339 of 1,339 player-weeks with max |delta| = 0.005, inside the module's own 0.011 tolerance. Stacking, answered from host stat lines rather than from docs: (1) PICK-SIX STACKS — the host emits pass_int and pass_int_td on the same line (3 real cases, e.g. player 4046 wk5: pass_int 1.0, pass_int_td 1.0), so under 2026 rates a pick-six costs -4.00 AND -2.00 = -6.00. (2) RECEPTION-DISTANCE BONUSES STACK ON THE BASE RECEPTION — the buckets partition the receptions (rec_0_4 + rec_5_9 + rec_10_19 + rec_20_29 + rec_30_39 + rec_40p == rec) and are paid in addition to rec x 0.08; an 8-catch line at 1/3/3/0/1/0 scores 0.64 + 4.61 = 5.25 before yardage. (3) ONE SACK PAYS EVERYTHING APPLICABLE — 194 host lines carry idp_sack together with idp_sack_yd, idp_tkl_solo, idp_tkl_ast, idp_tkl_loss, idp_qb_hit and often idp_ff / idp_fum_rec. The host also emits idp_tkl (combined), which carries no rate in this league, so solo+assist are not double-counted — a league that DID set idp_tkl would triple-count, and that would be Sleeper's behaviour too.

Both concepts ship under the same key 'displayValue'. On the live payload 19 of 51 asset legs across all 12 teams disagree with the board in DEFAULT market mode. reproduction.actual: market mode : 19/51 legs disagree with rankDerivedValue; worst: Travis Hunter shown=5637 board=4401 (+28.08%)

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A20-F06 identified the overlay/offense-only scale mix as a leagueAdjusted problem. findings.whatWorks: finder.py made this migration correctly: metadata.valueSource is stamped 'rankDerivedValue' on a live probe and unpriced assets are counted rather than dropped silently.
findings.rootCause: The offense-only board is a legitimate second value concept (an IDP-disabled re-run of the pipeline) but it is serialized into the field name the board value owns, so the response has no way to say which concept a number belongs to.
findings.requiredRepair: Either (a) drop the offense_only branch in _serialize_player and always emit rankDerivedValue, keeping offense-only for the internal _eff_val gap math only, or (b) emit it as a distinct key (offenseOnlyDisplayValue) plus a per-suggestion valueBasis stamp, and have trade-sections.jsx render the board value. Special-case the two-way players: max(offense, alt) must not be discardable by an offense-only re-read.
findings.dependencies: Fixing this also removes most of W29-F002's surface.

findings.title: valuationMode=leagueAdjusted is stamped on responses where 41% of asset legs are still priced on the unadjusted market board
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Mechanism, in one place: server.py::_valuation_scoped_contract fetches the league's factors and hands the engine a contract whose playersArray rows are already repriced. No engine knows the feature exists, because every engine reads exactly one value.' And: 'Every response stamps valuationMode - including "market". "This is the market board" and "this field is missing" must not read the same.'

Because suggestions.py serializes all-offense trades from that field (W29-F001), 21 of 51 legs (41.2%) across all 12 teams come back at the unadjusted market value while the response header says valuationMode: leagueAdjusted. For the 'Jason' roster it is 12 of 12 - the entire suggestion set. The same response's rosterAnalysis block IS adjusted, so one screen mixes both boards. The client-side applier is inconsistent with the server one: dynasty-data.js:1946-1948 additionally scales values.overall/finalAdjusted/displayValue and :1980 _finalAdjusted.

reproduction.command: OUT=/tmp/w29 bash docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W29/repro.sh

reproduction.actual: adjusted : 21/51 legs still at the UNADJUSTED offense-only market value

priorFinding.note: Prior identified the mechanism by code reading. Reproduced here at runtime across all 12 rosters with per-leg arithmetic: 21/51 legs, and 12/12 for one roster. Prior did not measure blast radius or note that the response stamps the mode it is not honouring.

findings.whatWorks: The lens itself is real and correct where it applies: 709/1092 rows carry a factor, monotonicityViolations is empty, and Jayden Daniels moves 8898 -> 9061 exactly as factor 1.018366 predicts. adjusted_rows correctly returns ALL rows rather than compact_ranks_and_tiers' ranked subset.

findings.requiredRepair: Scale offenseOnlyRankDerivedValue by the same factor in overlay.adjusted_rows (and mirror _offenseOnlyFinalAdjusted), OR remove the offense-only serialization per W29-F001. Add an assertion to the threading test that at least one served value differs between modes for a roster with known non-unit factors.

Stamp per-item source (rankHistory | current_fallback) on the rendered grade so a partially-covered trade says so. Ensure rank_history.jsonl is produced in production. findings.title: The league-adjusted board's scarcity is measured entirely in ROS log-rank units, so a 0-100 ordinal index sets the multiplier on every dynasty trade value under the adjusted lens
findings.claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: the valuation overlay is driven by 'positional scarcity from this league's 12 rosters'. It does not say the scarcity is measured in ROS units.
findings.observed: compute_scarcity reads value = float(p.get('rosValue')) for every rostered player (replacement.py:631) out of data/ros/team_strength/<league>.json, and measure_endogenous_starters solves the lineup over the same field. lineupScarcity is a RATIO of two rosValues, so it is dimensionless and no scale is mixed - but rosValue is 100*(ln(N+1)-ln(r))/ln(N+1), an ordinal log-rank index (ros/aggregate.py:171, gameplan.py:40-49). A ratio of two ordinal indices is not a cardinal 'drop from the top player to the last starter'. That ratio becomes factor = 1 + (lineupScarcity - 0.5)*0.20 (adjustment.py:247) and multiplies every dynasty value the engines serve. Live: WR lineupScarcity 0.634 -> factor 1.0268; DL 0.767 -> 1.0978; LB 0.598 -> 0.9797. replacement.py:20-52 documents the known bias honestly (projection path measures FLEX-TE share at 0.0% vs 10.4% on weekly actuals) but the docstring lives on the measurement function, not on the published board.

findings.userImpact: A user selecting the adjusted board gets every trade value multiplied by a number derived from rest-of-season ordinal ranks. The direction is plausible and bounded (MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT 0.25, observed +-4.5%), but the quantity is not the cardinal scarcity the name implies, and the /rankings toggle says nothing about ROS being its input.

findings.whatWorks: The coupling is dimensionally SAFE - a ratio of rosValues cancels units, so this is not the 0-9999-vs-0-100 error of W29-F005. Guardrails are real: evidence tier is STRUCTURAL_ONLY, absent axes contribute exactly 0, MAX_TOTAL_ADJUSTMENT clamps to +-25%, monotonicityViolations is empty on the live board, and docs/adjusted-board-backtest.md records that the adjusted board is deliberately a toggle rather than the default because four backtest framings found no improvement.
findings.rootCause: ROS is the only per-player quantity the platform has that is defined over a full roster including bench, so it is the only thing an endogenous lineup solve can run on. That is a real constraint, not an oversight.
findings.requiredRepair: Two separable steps. (1) Cheap and correct now: state the input in the overlay payload (a scarcityBasis: 'rosValue-ordinal' stamp) and in the /rankings toggle copy, so the lens does not read as board-derived. (2) The real fix: measure lineup scarcity from realized weekly scoring under the league's rate card - the same source scripts/measure_te_demand_actuals.py already uses - rather than from projection point estimates, which replacement.py itself shows understate flex demand for high-variance positions.
findings.dependencies: Step 2 depends on weekly actuals coverage; src/bdvm/actuals.py already scores nflverse weekly rows under exact league settings.
